neighbours.label: the word right before 'up' in a phrasal verb or compound (end up, catch up, close-up): predicts 'up'
fire: No matter how we plan the trip, we always end up getting lost.
After the break she had to work late to catch up on emails.
The photographer took a close-up of the bee on the flower.
If you skip the warm-up you may end up with a sore back.
He ran faster to keep up with the other runners.
They argued all evening but decided to make up before bed.
Somehow the quietest kid in class ended up as the mayor.
Please clean up the kitchen before your parents get home.
quiet: No matter how we plan the trip, the end is always the same.
After the break she had to work late to answer her emails.
The photographer took a picture of the bee on the flower.
If you skip the warm-up you may hurt your back.
He ran faster to stay with the other runners.
They argued all evening but decided to forgive each other before bed.
Somehow the quietest kid in class became the mayor.
Please wash the dishes before your parents get home.

notes: Card: peaks on ' end' x7, ' make', ' ended', ' close'(-up), ' catch'(up), each followed by 'up'; the output direction strongly suppresses ' up' (it fires where 'up' comes next). Near misses use the same verbs without a following 'up'.
